Thus, the basic plea of the Petitioner is for extension of time by three months to submit the documents in support of possession of ownership or lease rights or land use rights of 50% of the land required for the capacity for which connectivity is sought, as the Petitioner’s Project was affected by the reclassification of the b. On account of the uncertainty of the land on which the Project is to be constructed, the Petitioner seeks protection from any coercive/ precipitative action by CTUIL, penalty or payment of transmission charges in terms of the 2020 Sharing Regulations, along with retention of in-principle connectivity granted by CTUIL to the Petitioner for 140 MW at Davangere Sub-station. f. The Petitioner made a representation to CTUIL regarding the issues faced by the Petitioner in the development of the Project. However, the Petitioner is yet to receive any response from CTUIL. Therefore, the Petitioner has filed the instant petition. l. The Petitioner acted on the representation(s) given by CTUIL by way of its consultation meetings, along with the material documents and studies, such as the CEA Report available in the public domain, with respect to connectivity being available at Davangere Sub-station. Hence, under these circumstances, the Petitioner is not at fault at all, and no liability or penalty can be imposed upon the Petitioner. m. The Petitioner, on 20.7.2024, issued an email to CTUIL requesting a meeting to discuss the aforesaid issue of the Davangere region. However, the Petitioner did not receive a response from CTUIL. q. The Petitioner is yet to receive any communication from CTUIL on the subject issue. Therefore, there is a strong apprehension that CTUIL may not consider the representation made by the Petitioner and/ or take any step(s) against the Petitioner, which are coercive/ precipitative and prejudicial in nature and would be legally and commercially detrimental to its interest. v. The Commission has exercised its inherent powers to relax provided under Regulation 41 of the 2022 GNA Regulations on account of reasons beyond the control of the affected party in order dated 21.1.2024 in Petition (Diary) No. 20 of 2024, order dated 31.1.2024 in Petition No. 18/MP/2024 and in order dated 31.1.2024 in Petition No. 19/MP/2024 under Regulation 8.2 (c) of the 2022 GNA Regulations on account of the reasons beyond their control. The Commission should grant a similar relief to the Petitioner in the present case since it is a fit case of _force majeure_ and is on account of the factors which are beyond the reasonable control of the Petitioner. invoke and encash the Conn-BGs, thereby causing significant financial hardship to the Petitioner despite the delay being due to a _force majeure_ event. Despite being severely affected by the _force majeure_ event, the Petitioner remains committed to commissioning the Project on time and has taken reasonable steps towards the implementation of the Project. Substantial progress has been made towards implementing the Project, and significant financial commitments have already been undertaken in furtherance thereof. e. CTUIL has neither filed any reply on merits nor opposed the Petitioner’s plea regarding the delay in the implementation of the Project on account of the _force majeure_ event. The absence of any rebuttal or contest from CTUIL on this material aspect is significant. It can reasonably be inferred that CTUIL itself is uncertain about the implications of the said re-classification and, by necessary implication, acknowledges that the Petitioner has indeed been adversely impacted by this unforeseen and uncontrollable event. CTUIL’s silence strengthens the Petitioner’s contention that the delay is attributable solely to circumstances beyond its control and that the Petitioner cannot be penalised for the same. j.
